questions.stem: Notebook users complain that Spark sessions take minutes to start. The workspace uses a custom pool for small, interactive jobs. What change gives the fastest session start?

options.text: Increase the custom pool's maximum node count
Turn off autoscale on the custom pool
Use the starter pool, whose clusters are kept ready
Move the notebooks into a different workspace

questions.explanation: Starter pools are kept warm by Fabric, so sessions usually start in seconds. Custom pools start their nodes on demand, which takes longer, and changing their size doesn't change that.

questions.stem: Every notebook in a workspace needs the same Python libraries and Spark properties. How do you provide them by default?

options.text: Put the libraries in a lakehouse Files folder
Paste the same %pip install cell at the top of every notebook
Install the libraries on each developer's PC
Attach an environment with those libraries and properties as the workspace's default environment

questions.explanation: An environment holds libraries and Spark settings, and choosing it as the workspace default in the workspace's Spark settings applies it to notebooks and Spark job definitions that don't pick another.

questions.stem: Which three can you set when you create a custom Spark pool for a workspace? Each correct answer is part of the solution.

options.text: The KQL cache period
The Git branch the pool uses
Dynamic executor allocation
Autoscale with a minimum and maximum number of nodes
The node size

questions.explanation: A custom pool sets its node size, autoscale range and whether executors are allocated dynamically. Cache periods belong to KQL databases and branches to Git integration.

questions.stem: Several notebooks run one after another for the same user and each waits for its own Spark session. Which workspace setting lets them share a session?

options.text: High concurrency mode
Workspace identity
Starter pool autoscale
Delta auto-optimize

questions.explanation: High concurrency mode lets several notebooks share one Spark session, so later notebooks start without waiting for a new session.

questions.stem: A data engineer with the Contributor role tries to change the default Spark pool in a workspace's settings but can't. Which workspace role do they need?

options.text: Member
Viewer
Contributor with Reshare permission
Admin

questions.explanation: Only workspace admins can change the workspace's Apache Spark settings. Member and Contributor can build items but not change these settings.

questions.stem: A workspace admin wants to create a custom Spark pool, but the option isn't available. What must happen first?

options.text: The workspace admin publishes a default environment for the workspace
A capacity admin enables Customized workspace pools in the Spark Compute section of the capacity settings
A Fabric admin assigns the workspace to a domain that allows custom pools
The workspace admin turns on high concurrency mode for notebooks

questions.explanation: Custom pools depend on the capacity-level Customized workspace pools control. Domains, environments and high concurrency don't unlock custom pools.

questions.stem: A workspace admin turns on Set maximum job lifetime to stop runaway Spark jobs. Which two kinds of work can this setting stop? Each correct answer is a complete solution.

options.text: A scheduled notebook run started by a pipeline
A Spark job definition run started by a user
A materialized lake view refresh
Platform security and policy enforcement operations
Lakehouse table maintenance such as optimize and vacuum

questions.explanation: The limit applies only to user-submitted jobs such as notebook runs, including pipeline-orchestrated runs, and Spark job definition runs. System-managed jobs such as table maintenance and materialized lake view refreshes run to completion.

questions.stem: Analysts say their interactive notebook sessions expire too soon during long investigations. Where does a workspace admin change how long interactive sessions last?

options.text: The retention period in the workspace's OneLake settings
The runtime version in the workspace's default environment
The node size of the starter pool in the Pool tab
The Spark session timeout in the workspace's Jobs settings

questions.explanation: The Jobs settings include a Spark session timeout for all interactive notebook sessions, which defaults to 20 minutes. Node size, runtime and OneLake retention don't control session expiry.

questions.stem: A team runs only small Spark workloads and wants the cheapest custom pool where the driver and executor share one node. How do you configure the pool?

options.text: Set the minimum number of nodes to one
Turn on dynamic allocation with a maximum of zero executors
Choose the XX-Large node size and turn off autoscale
Turn on high concurrency mode and keep the starter pool

questions.explanation: Setting the minimum node count to one creates a single node pool in which the driver and executor run on one node. The other options don't create a single node pool.

questions.stem: An environment uses Quick mode to install PyPI libraries. A Spark job definition that uses the environment can't import them, but notebooks can. Why?

options.text: Quick mode installs only R libraries
Quick mode libraries apply only after the capacity restarts
Quick mode works only with notebooks, not Spark job definitions
Quick mode requires the starter pool to be turned off

questions.explanation: Quick mode installs libraries at session start for notebooks only. Spark job definitions need the libraries in Full mode.
